Italian, local and international newspapers, with translation into Italian. For Windows, fully keyboard-driven and with NVDA. Free.

KILLA NEWS is Killa Records' digital newsstand for Windows 10 and 11. It brings together Italian, international and local newspapers in a single program. It is designed for blind and visually impaired people and for anyone who uses NVDA or another screen reader: every feature works from the keyboard, without a mouse. It is free. The program is in Italian.

Your favourite newspapers, saved articles and settings stay where they are.
You can check whenever you like from the Killa Records menu, item “Controlla aggiornamenti di KILLA NEWS” (Check for updates). You can also turn off the automatic check in the Settings.

Discover Killa Records, its founder and the beta tester team.
Behind Killa Records there is a person, an idea and a dream.
Killa Records is an independent project that brings together music, creativity, technology and accessibility.
. I am a young Moroccan man who has lived in Italy since 2017, and I have turned my passion for music, creativity and technology into something I dream of growing every day.

Music is an important part of my life. I write songs, experiment with new genres and pursue my artistic path under the name Abdu Killa. But I don't want to stop at music: I also love creating, designing and giving shape to new ideas.

I am blind, and this is part of my story. Over time I have learned to face obstacles and difficulties, but I have also developed a strong focus on accessibility and on the possibilities that technology offers. I believe creativity should have no barriers and that everyone should be able to take part, express themselves and carry out their own projects.
, an independent project that brings together two worlds: Killa Records Music, dedicated to music and artists, and Killa Records Games, dedicated to video game development and accessible experiences.
I don't see Killa Records only as a brand, but as a dream I want to build step by step, making room for ideas, collaborations and talent.

Privacy and cookie policy for the Killa Records Games website and the game Il Mio Bar.
, who runs the Killa Records Games website (killarecordsgames.com) under the artist name Killa. For any request, write to

The website does not use cookies and does not show advertising. For technical and security reasons, the server hosting the website may record the IP address and time of access, as happens with every website.

To know how many people visit the website we use GoatCounter, a privacy-friendly statistics service. It does not use cookies, does not identify you and does not build a profile about you. It only records generic data: the page visited, the site you came from, the type of browser and system, the screen size and the approximate country. Your IP address is not stored. You can find out more at

If you write to us using the form on the Contact page, your name, your email and your message are saved in the website's database (Supabase service) and read only by the data controller, in order to reply to you. You can ask at any time for them to be deleted by writing to
. If you write to us directly by email, we use your address and message only to reply to you.

Il Mio Bar can be played without creating an account. In that case the save stays only on your device, in the program's memory (local storage). We do not receive it and cannot see it. If you delete the program's or website's data from your device, the save disappears.

If you create an account, we need your email address and a password, to confirm the address, let you sign in and keep your online saves. The data is stored with the Supabase service, which provides us with storage and account access. We cannot read your password. We keep the data for as long as the account exists: you can ask for it to be deleted at any time.

In multiplayer games, the name you choose, the scores and the chat messages pass through a real-time service and are visible to the other players in the room. We do not keep them in an archive. Do not write personal data in the chat.

Taking part in the weekly leaderboards of Il Mio Bar and Global Manager is optional. If you choose to take part from the Leaderboards page, we keep the nickname you provide, linked to your game account, and every week a snapshot of your starting in-game value (the bar's cash or the verified wealth) to calculate how much you have earned. Only the nickname and the scores are shown publicly; the winner of each week remains in the page's hall of fame. Weekly snapshots are deleted after about two months. You can change your nickname or leave the leaderboard at any time from the same page; once you leave, your nickname no longer appears in the current leaderboard. To also remove your nickname from the hall of fame, write to us from the Contact page.
The administration page is reserved for the data controller. It uses an email and password sign-in managed by Supabase.
Killa Assistant, the artificial intelligence chat

On the website you can, if you wish, use Killa Assistant: a virtual assistant based on artificial intelligence, not a person. Before the chat starts we show you a notice. Do not write personal data in your messages (name, address, phone, email, passwords, payment details, documents, health).

To generate the replies, the messages of the conversation pass through our Supabase service and are sent to Groq, the artificial intelligence provider we use. Groq may also process data in the United States, according to its own terms and data processing agreement, and is not allowed to use the messages to train its models. We do not save the content of conversations.

To prevent abuse we limit the number of messages: to do this we keep, for about 24 hours, an anonymous code calculated from your IP address with a non-reversible process, together with the time of the message. We do not save the IP address.

If you subscribe to the newsletter, we process your email address to send you Killa Records news: games and apps, music releases, news and announcements, plus a welcome email after you subscribe. The legal basis is your consent, which you give by ticking the box in the form and confirming your subscription with the link you receive by email (double opt-in).

To manage the newsletter we use Brevo (Sendinblue SAS, France, European Union), which processes the data on our behalf as data processor. Brevo may record whether you open the emails and click the links, to give us statistics on the mailings. To avoid sending the welcome email twice, we keep a non-reversible fingerprint of your address, not the address itself.

You can unsubscribe at any time with the “Cancellati dalla newsletter” (Unsubscribe) link at the bottom of every email, or by writing to info@killarecordsgames.com. We keep your address for as long as you remain subscribed; after you unsubscribe we no longer write to you.
KILLA NEWS works without an account. The news is downloaded directly from the newspapers' websites; favourites, history and settings stay on your computer.

To understand how many people use the app and which sections are most useful, KILLA NEWS sends Killa Records: a random code created at first start-up, which does not contain your name, your email or data about your computer; the program version; the type of installation (installed or portable); how many times the program is opened and how many times the sections and some features, such as translation and sharing, are used. We do not send titles, articles read, searches or other content, and we do not save the IP address. The legal basis is our legitimate interest in improving the app. The data is kept for a maximum of 13 months in the Supabase database, which manages it on our behalf, and only the administrator can see it. You can turn off sending at any time in the KILLA NEWS Settings, checkbox “Invia statistiche anonime d'uso” (Send anonymous usage statistics).

When you ask to translate an article, its text is sent to Google's translation service (Google Translate) or, if it does not respond, to MyMemory (Translated srl, Italy). Only the text of the article is sent, not data about you.

To check whether a new version exists, KILLA NEWS contacts GitHub (GitHub Inc., United States), which, like any website, receives the computer's IP address. When you share an article, KILLA NEWS opens WhatsApp or your email program with the text already written: you choose whether and to whom to send it.
Cookies and data on your device

The games only use the device's local storage to remember saves and settings, such as the screen reader and touch controls. This is technical data needed for them to work and is not used to track you.
You can ask us what data we hold about you, and ask us to correct it, download it or delete it, including accounts and online saves. Write to
stating the email you used to create the account. You also have the right to lodge a complaint with the Italian Data Protection Authority (Garante per la protezione dei dati personali).
If the processing changes, we will update this page and the date at the top.
